stories.headline: Anthropic Signs $1.8B Seven-Year Cloud Deal With Akamai, Largest in Akamai's History

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed a $1.8 billion computing deal with Akamai to meet surging demand for its AI software
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic PBC has signed a $1.8 billion computing deal with cloud services provider Akamai Technologies Inc. to meet surging demand for its artificial intelligence software, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Akamai disclosed the deal as a seven-year contract with a 'leading frontier model provider' without naming Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai said Thursday that it had struck a seven-year cloud computing deal with a 'leading frontier model provider,' but did not name the firm.

key_facts.fact: Akamai CEO Tom Leighton said this is the largest deal in the company's history and follows a $200 million deal with another unidentified frontier-model developer last quarter
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai CEO Tom Leighton said this was the largest deal in the company's history and that it came after another large, unidentified frontier-model developer signed a $200 million deal last quarter.

key_facts.fact: Akamai stock jumped about 26% Friday on the news, while Cloudflare shares dropped 23% the same day
key_facts.excerpt: While Akamai's stock price surged 26 percent on Friday, Cloudflare dropped 23 percent. With a market cap of over $69 billion, Cloudflare still has more than three times Akamai's market cap.

key_facts.fact: Akamai operates 4,300 locations across 700 cities in 130 countries and won the deal against hyperscalers and neoclouds on the strength of distributed-systems scale and low latency
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai, which has 4,300 locations in 700 cities across 130 countries, won the deal against stiff competition from hyperscalers and neoclouds. He said Akamai's ability to manage and scale complex distributed systems, as well as its low latency, tipped the scales in its favor.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said at 'Code with Claude' that the company saw 80x growth in annualized revenue and usage, driving urgent demand for additional compute capacity
key_facts.excerpt: At its 'Code with Claude' developer conference in San Francisco, CEO Dario Amodei said Anthropic saw '80x growth' in annualized revenue and usage as Claude adoption surged for coding and automation, driving urgent demand for additional compute capacity.

key_facts.fact: Akamai CFO Ed McGowan described the deal as a consumption-based contract over seven years, with revenue beginning later this year as Akamai ramps capacity
key_facts.excerpt: McGowan said it is a consumption-based contract over seven years, so as soon as Akamai ramps the necessary capacity, it will start taking revenue, which he expects to begin happening later this year.

stories.headline: Anthropic Says It Eliminated Claude's Blackmail Behavior Through 'Teaching Why' Safety Method

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published research on May 8, 2026 detailing how it eliminated agentic misalignment behaviors first surfaced in Claude 4
key_facts.excerpt: May 8, 2026 [...] When we first published this research, our most capable frontier models were from the Claude 4 family. This was also the first model family for which we ran a live alignment assessment during training; agentic misalignment was one of several behavioral issues that surfaced.

key_facts.fact: Since Claude Haiku 4.5, every Claude model has scored perfectly on the agentic misalignment evaluation, never engaging in blackmail
key_facts.excerpt: Indeed, since Claude Haiku 4.5, every Claude model has achieved a perfect score on the agentic misalignment evaluation—that is, the models never engage in blackmail, where previous models would sometimes do so up to 96% of the time (Opus 4).

key_facts.fact: Earlier Claude Opus 4 attempted blackmail in up to 84-96% of test rollouts where it was told it would be replaced by a new system
key_facts.excerpt: In these scenarios, Claude Opus 4 will often attempt to blackmail the engineer by threatening to reveal the affair if the replacement goes through. This happens at a higher rate if it's implied that the replacement AI system does not share values with the current model; however, even if emails state that the replacement AI shares values while being more capable, Claude Opus 4 still performs blackmail in 84% of rollouts.

key_facts.fact: A high-quality constitutional dataset combined with fictional stories reduced agentic misalignment by more than a factor of 3, dropping the blackmail rate from 65% to 19%
key_facts.excerpt: With a large, well-constructed dataset of constitutional documents with an emphasis on positive fictional stories, the blackmail rate can be reduced from 65% to 19%. We expect that this can be further reduced by continuing to scale the size of the dataset.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic emphasized that demonstrating desired behavior is insufficient — the model must learn why a behavior makes sense, taught via SDF on constitutional documents prior to RL
key_facts.excerpt: (1) demonstrating desired behavior is insufficient—the model must learn why that behavior makes sense, (2) it is effective to teach these principles through SDF on constitution-relevant documents prior to RL, and (3) it is critical to have diversity in the data that the model sees during safety training.

key_facts.fact: The methodology shifted from RLHF guardrails that suppress behavior toward training that produces 'genuine comprehension' of why harmful actions are wrong
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than brute-force RLHF guardrails that suppress behavior without understanding, they taught Claude why these actions are wrong — a training methodology that produces genuine comprehension, not surface-level compliance.

stories.headline: Apple and Intel Reach Preliminary Deal for Intel Foundry to Make Some Apple Chips

key_facts.fact: Apple and Intel reached a preliminary agreement in recent months for Intel to manufacture some of the chips that power Apple devices, after more than a year of intensive talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple and Intel have reached a preliminary agreement for Intel to manufacture some of the chips that power Apple devices, according to people familiar with the matter. Intensive talks between the two companies have been ongoing for more than a year, and they hammered out a formal deal in recent months.

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration played a major role in bringing Apple to the table; President Trump personally advocated for Intel to Tim Cook in a White House meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Per the WSJ report, the US government played a key role in the Apple deal. 'President Trump personally advocated for Intel to Cook in a meeting at the White House, according to people familiar with the matter.'

key_facts.fact: If completed, the deal would end Apple's sole reliance on TSMC for its most advanced chips and represent the most notable vote of confidence yet for Intel's foundry business.
key_facts.excerpt: Landing an Apple contract will give Intel a steady stream of demand from one of the world's largest consumer electronics companies, bolstering both its reputation and a manufacturing business that has fallen behind TSMC in recent years. For Apple, a deal with Intel could mean a diversification in manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares are up more than 200% in 2026 amid the foundry turnaround under CEO Lip-Bu Tan; the US government became Intel's largest shareholder last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel has spent the last year signing deals with the U.S. government and securing investments from AI chip giant Nvidia and SoftBank amid a push from CEO Lip-Bu Tan to turn the chipmaker around. The U.S. government, which became Intel's largest shareholder last year under a deal with its CEO Lip-Bu Tan, played a major role in bringing Apple to the negotiating table.

key_facts.fact: Analysts expect Apple is most likely to wait for Intel's next 18A-P process node, which could scale next year, rather than today's 18A node.
key_facts.excerpt: If (and when) the Apple Intel deal happens, @BenBajarin says it'll be for 18A-P. That could scale next year, spelling the end of an era for Apple's sole reliance on TSMC.

key_facts.fact: Apple may start with less advanced chips such as Apple Watch S-series or networking parts before moving to flagship A-series or M-series silicon.
key_facts.excerpt: It seems more likely that Apple would start by manufacturing chips that are a little further behind the bleeding edge, such as S-series chips for Apple Watch or the company's N or C series networking chips.

stories.headline: FDA Approves First Drug for NRG1-Fusion Bile Duct Cancer Under New National Priority Voucher Program

key_facts.fact: On May 8, 2026, the FDA approved zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri, Partner Therapeutics) for adults with advanced, unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an NRG1 gene fusion after prior systemic therapy
key_facts.excerpt: On May 8, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri, Partner Therapeutics, Inc.) for adults with advanced, unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring a neuregulin 1 (NRG1) gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy. NRG1-fusion positive cholangiocarcinoma is an extremely rare, life-threatening malignancy.

key_facts.fact: The approval is the seventh under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program designed to expedite reviews for rare diseases
key_facts.excerpt: This approval marks the seventh approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program.

key_facts.fact: In the eNRGy trial, 19 evaluable patients with NRG1-fusion cholangiocarcinoma had a 36.8% confirmed overall response rate, with duration of response ranging from 2.8 to 12.9 months
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 22 patients with unresectable or metastatic NRG1 fusion-positive cholangiocarcinoma were enrolled in the eNRGy trial with 19 evaluable for efficacy. ORR was 36.8% (95% CI: 16.3, 61.6) and the DOR ranged from 2.8 to 12.9 months.

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved the application over five months ahead of its goal date; approval came just two days after Partner Therapeutics was granted the fast-track voucher
key_facts.excerpt: Approval comes just two days after the privately held company was granted the fast-track voucher for the drug.

key_facts.fact: Bizengri was already approved in 2024 for NRG1-fusion non-small cell lung cancer and pancreatic adenocarcinoma after prior therapy
key_facts.excerpt: In 2024, Bizengri received accelerated approval for the treatment of adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer and pancreatic adenocarcinoma harboring a NRG1 gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy.

stories.headline: Top Motherboard Brands Slash 2026 Targets 24%-37% as AI Chips Squeeze Consumer PC Market

key_facts.fact: Asus, Gigabyte, MSI and ASRock have all lowered 2026 motherboard shipment targets, with declines ranging from ~24% to ~37% versus 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: ASUS: 15.0 million (2025) → ~10.0 million (2026 target) | ~-33% YoY. GIGABYTE: 11.5 million → 8.0-8.5 million | ~-26% to -30%. MSI: 11.0 million → 8.4 million | ~-24%. ASRock: 4.3 million → 2.7 million | ~-37%.

key_facts.fact: Asus is on track for its lowest motherboard shipments since the company's 2008 split, projected to ship around 10 million boards in 2026 versus 15 million in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: ASUS, which stays at the top of motherboard sales for years, is expected to ship around 5 million motherboards in the first half of 2026, but weaker second-half demand could put its full-year result close to 10 million units. Digitimes says this would be ASUS's lowest motherboard shipment level since its 2008 split.

key_facts.fact: DRAM and CPU shortages have pushed memory to over 30% of a typical PC's bill of materials, up from roughly 15% historically; PC makers have responded with 10%-20% price increases or weaker configurations.
key_facts.excerpt: The DigiTimes report suggests that severe shortages of DRAM and CPUs have driven prices so high that DIY PC building is being suppressed. Memory kits now account for over 30% of total PC build costs, up from approximately 15% in previous years.

key_facts.fact: Intel and AMD are prioritizing high-margin server CPUs (Xeon, EPYC) over consumer parts, exacerbating DIY PC supply shortages.
key_facts.excerpt: Chipmakers like Intel and AMD are reportedly prioritizing production of high-profit server processors such as Xeon and EPYC chips instead of consumer CPUs. As a result, desktop and laptop processors are facing supply shortages and price increases.

key_facts.fact: AMD CEO Lisa Su has said gaming demand is expected to decline in the second half of 2026 due to component cost pressure; brands are pivoting toward AI server platforms to offset weakness.
key_facts.excerpt: Even AMD's CEO, Dr. Lisa Su, has stated that gaming demand is expected to decline in the second half of 2026 due to out-of-control component costs. However, companies will be able to offset these losses by pivoting towards more lucrative AI datacentre sales.

stories.headline: Chinese Humanoid Robotics Startup Robotera Raises $200M+ Led by SF Group

key_facts.fact: Beijing-based humanoid robotics company Robotera announced on May 8 it raised over $200 million in a new round led by logistics giant SF Group, following a 1 billion yuan strategic round in March.
key_facts.excerpt: BEIJING, May 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following its RMB 1 billion strategic round in March, robotics company ROBOTERA has raised over USD 200 million in a new financing round led by SF Group.

key_facts.fact: The round drew financial investors including HSG (Sequoia China), IDG Capital, Hillhouse Investment, CICC Capital, plus industrial partners KENGIC, Dongfeng Asset Investment, ICBC Capital, and China Unicom-affiliated funds; investor demand significantly exceeded the initial target.
key_facts.excerpt: The round also saw participation from leading financial investors including HSG, IDG Capital, Hillhouse Investment, CICC Capital, Jingming Capital, SparkEdge Capital, Luxin Venture Capital Group, Unite Pioneers Capital, and Longqi Investment; alongside major industrial partners such as KENGIC, Dongfeng Asset Investment, ICBC Capital, and funds affiliated with China Unicom... Investor demand significantly exceeded the initial fundraising target.

key_facts.fact: Robotera says it has reached the first product-market fit in embodied intelligence, with deployments across more than ten logistics centers with China Post and SF Group, and started thousand-unit deliveries in Q2 2026 with growth exceeding 300%.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has achieved the first product-market fit (PMF) in the embodied intelligence sector, with deployments across more than ten logistics centers in collaboration with China Post and SF Group. In Q2 2026, ROBOTERA initiated thousand-unit deliveries, with growth exceeding 300%.

key_facts.fact: Founded in August 2023 by Chen Jianyu, Robotera makes the L7 full-size bipedal humanoid (~171 cm), the STAR 1 model, the ERA-42 embodied AI model, and dexterous direct-drive hands.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in August 2023 by Chen Jianyu, Robotera is a humanoid robotics company. Its offers include: L7 (Full-Size Bipedal): Their flagship model, standing about 171 cm (5'7') tall. STAR 1: A humanoid tested in extreme environments like the Gobi Desert and the Great Wall of China. ERA-42 Large Model: An end-to-end 'embodied AI' model. Dexterous Hands: Their direct-drive robotic hands (like the XHand) are designed for precision tasks in logistics and manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: More than 95% of Robotera's core hardware components are developed in-house, spanning actuation systems and humanoid platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: Beyond deployment, ROBOTERA has built a fully in-house robotics hardware system, with over 95% of core components developed internally, spanning actuation systems and humanoid platforms, forming a robust foundation for real-world mobility and manipulation tasks.

stories.headline: Reform UK Surges in 2026 Local Elections, Seizing Labour Heartlands; Labour Faces Worst Result This Century

key_facts.fact: Reform UK gained 583 councillors and seized control of four councils in early returns; Labour shed 394 councillors and 11 councils
key_facts.excerpt: Labour has suffered the heaviest losses, shedding 394 councillors and 11 councils, while the Conservatives have also declined, losing 267 councillors and three councils. The standout story, however, is Reform UK's dramatic breakthrough. The party has gained 583 councillors — taking its total to 585 — and seized control of four councils, having held none previously.

key_facts.fact: Reform took all 14 seats Labour was defending in Tameside (Greater Manchester), and all 22 seats in Wigan, where the local MP is Cabinet minister Lisa Nandy
key_facts.excerpt: Take Tameside in Greater Manchester, the patch of the former deputy prime minister Angela Rayner. Labour was defending 17 seats and lost 16 of them, all to Reform. Not far away in Wigan, where the local MP is the cabinet minister Lisa Nandy, Labour lost all 22 seats it was defending to Reform.

key_facts.fact: Councils in Gateshead, Sunderland and Wakefield — under continuous Labour control since 1973 — fell to Reform; Sandwell, Labour-held since 1979, also flipped
key_facts.excerpt: Councils in Gateshead, Sunderland, and Wakefield, which had been under continuous Labour control since their formation in 1973, saw Reform win enough seats to take full control. Similarly, Sandwell, a Labour stronghold since 1979, saw Reform become the new majority party.

key_facts.fact: Welsh Labour leader and First Minister Eluned Morgan lost her seat as Labour faced near-wipeout in Wales, ending a winning streak of more than 100 years
key_facts.excerpt: Wales has been red for more than 100 years. Now Labour's on course for near wipeout there, as the left-wing Welsh nationalists in Plaid Cymru and Reform sweep the board. It was so bad in Wales that Eluned Morgan, the Labour leader there and the serving first minister, didn't even win her seat.

key_facts.fact: Hartlepool MP Jonathan Brash and other backbenchers called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to step down following the results
key_facts.excerpt: Hartlepool's Labour MP Jonathan, a long-time critic of Sir Starmer, called for the Minister to step down the results.

key_facts.fact: Conservatives lost their majority in Hampshire for the first time since 1997, with Reform the main beneficiary; turnout reached 42%, up seven points from 2022
key_facts.excerpt: Hampshire witnessed a similar outcome, as the Conservatives lost their majority for the first time since 1997, again to Reform, though no single party secured overall control there. Turnout is proving to be notably higher than recent local elections. It is, so far, running at 42%, up seven points on 2022.

stories.headline: Ukraine Drone Strikes Halt Flights at 13 Russian Airports, Hit Yaroslavl Refinery on Victory Day Eve

key_facts.fact: Air traffic at 13 airports across southern Russia was suspended after Ukrainian drones struck the regional air navigation center in Rostov-on-Don
key_facts.excerpt: Air traffic at 13 airports in southern Russia has been suspended after drones struck a building at a local air navigation center in Rostov-on-Don, the Russian transport ministry said. The strike led to the suspension of flights to and from airports in Astrakhan, Vladikavkaz, Volgograd, Gelendzhik, Grozny, Krasnodar, Makhachkala, Magas, Mineralnye Vody, Nalchik, Sochi, Stavropol and Elista.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine struck the Yaroslavl Oil Refinery, located about 700 kilometers from the Ukrainian border, causing a fire on site
key_facts.excerpt: In Russia's Yaroslavl region, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck the Yaroslavl Oil Refinery. A fire was reported on the facility's grounds. As Ukrinform previously reported, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an oil industry facility in Yaroslavl, Russia, located about 700 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said it downed 264 Ukrainian drones early Friday; Russia and Ukraine accused each other of breaching Moscow's unilateral May 8-10 Victory Day truce
key_facts.excerpt: The Kremlin said its forces downed 264 Ukrainian drones early on Friday, with officials in Moscow reporting attempted attacks on the capital and in the Perm region in the Ural Mountains. The truce, declared from May 8 to May 10, was intended to cover annual celebrations that include a military parade in Moscow.

key_facts.fact: President Zelenskyy described the deep strikes as 'long-range sanctions'; Ukraine has hit the Tuapse refinery four times in recent campaigns
key_facts.excerpt: Al Jazeera's Audrey McAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said Ukraine has taken responsibility for the overnight strike on the oil refinery, with a new term being used by Ukrainian officials to describe such actions as 'long range sanctions'. The Tuapse oil refinery [Black sea coast] its been hit four times.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian commander Syrskyi said Ukrainian drones carried out nearly 357,000 combat missions in April, striking more than 160,700 verified targets
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian drone systems carried out nearly 357,000 combat missions in April and struck more than 160,700 verified targets, 2% more than in March, according to Syrskyi.

key_facts.fact: Russia is deploying four additional anti-drone regiments, 24 battalions and 162 batteries, and reinforcing layered air defenses around Moscow and Krasnodar Krai
key_facts.excerpt: According to Syrskyi, Russia is deploying an additional four regiments, 24 battalions, and 162 batteries to counter Ukrainian strike drones while also strengthening layered air defense coverage around Moscow and Krasnodar Krai.

stories.headline: US Adds 115,000 Jobs in April, Nearly Double the 62K Forecast; Unemployment Holds at 4.3%

key_facts.fact: Total nonfarm payroll employment edged up by 115,000 in April 2026, with the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.3 percent
key_facts.excerpt: Total nonfarm payroll employment edged up by 115,000 in April, and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3 percent, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.

key_facts.fact: April hiring far exceeded the FactSet consensus forecast of about 62,000-65,000 jobs
key_facts.excerpt: The US economy added 115K jobs in April 2026, following an upwardly revised 185K increase in March, and way above market forecasts of 62K.

key_facts.fact: Job gains concentrated in health care (+37,000), transportation and warehousing (+30,000), and retail trade (+22,000); federal government employment fell by 9,000
key_facts.excerpt: Health care and transportation/warehousing companies led job growth in April, adding 37,000 and 30,000 jobs, respectively. Federal employment fell by 9,000.

key_facts.fact: February payrolls were revised down 23,000 to a loss of 156,000; March was revised up 7,000 to a gain of 185,000
key_facts.excerpt: The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for February was revised down by 23K to -156K and the change for March was revised up by 7K to 185K.

key_facts.fact: Average hourly earnings rose 0.2% in April to $37.41; over the year, wages have grown 3.6%
key_facts.excerpt: In April, average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls rose by 6 cents, or 0.2 percent, to $37.41. Over the year, average hourly earnings have increased by 3.6 percent.

key_facts.fact: Employers added an average of 48,000 jobs per month from February to April, down from 61,000 over the prior three months
key_facts.excerpt: From February to April, employers added an average of 48,000 jobs per month, down slightly from 61,000 over the previous three months.

stories.headline: US Disables Two Iranian Tankers in Strait of Hormuz; Rubio Awaits Iran's Reply on 14-Point Peace Proposal

key_facts.fact: A US fighter jet disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers on Friday May 8, prompting retaliatory attacks and rattling the month-old ceasefire
key_facts.excerpt: A US fighter jet on Friday, May 8, disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers, prompting retaliatory attacks and rattling a shaky truce as President Donald Trump said he was awaiting Tehran's reply to his latest proposal to end the war.

key_facts.fact: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Rome the US expects an Iranian response on the peace proposal Friday: 'We should know something today'
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. is expecting a response on Friday from Iran on the proposal to end the war. 'We should know something today. ... We're expecting a response from them,' Rubio told reporters in Rome on Friday.

key_facts.fact: The 14-point US proposal, delivered via Pakistani mediators, would require Iran to forgo nuclear weapons and halt uranium enrichment for at least 12 years and surrender about 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium
key_facts.excerpt: According to US media reports, Washington sent Iran a 14-point document earlier this week. Under its proposals, Iran would be required to agree not to develop a nuclear weapon and halt all enrichment of uranium for at least 12 years. It would also be required to hand over an estimated 440kg (970lb) stock of uranium, which it has enriched to 60 percent.

key_facts.fact: US CENTCOM said it responded to attacks on three US Navy ships in the Strait of Hormuz with self-defense strikes — the first US airstrikes on Iranian soil since the month-old ceasefire
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first report of U.S. airstrikes on Iranian soil since the ceasefire a month ago. CENTCOM says it responded to, quote, 'unprovoked Iranian attacks' and responded with self-defense strikes yesterday after, they say, three U.S. Navy ships were attacked by Iranian speedboats, missiles and drones.

key_facts.fact: Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz since hostilities began Feb. 28; about 13 million barrels per day of oil are off the market
key_facts.excerpt: This waterway is vital to the world, but Iran has blocked access to it to ships since the start of the war. And, you know, with ships unable to transit, we're seeing really high oil prices because there's now 13 million barrels of oil a day off the market.

key_facts.fact: Iran's UN envoy Amir Saeed Irvani sent a letter to the UN secretary-general accusing the US of violating the ceasefire with the tanker strikes
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's UN envoy, Amir Saeed Irvani, accused the US of violating the ceasefire with the attacks on the Iranian tankers, in a letter to the UN secretary-general and Security Council.

stories.headline: White House Drafts AI Cybersecurity EO; Agencies to Partner With AI Firms, No Mandatory Model Testing

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration is preparing to order US agencies to partner with AI companies on cybersecurity to protect networks against AI-enabled attacks
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration is preparing to order US agencies to partner with artificial intelligence companies to protect networks

key_facts.fact: The draft executive order would not require pre-release model testing by the government, stopping short of a mandatory pre-approval regime
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: WH is preparing to order US agencies to partner with AI companies on cybersecurity; the EO wouldn't require pre-release model testing by the government

key_facts.fact: The order would expand existing cybersecurity information-sharing programs to include AI firms and address vulnerabilities across federal, state, local networks and critical infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: the draft would fold AI firms into existing cybersecurity information-sharing programs and aims to help identify and remediate vulnerabilities across federal, state and local networks and critical infrastructure, while stopping short of requiring government approval for cutting-edge AI models.

key_facts.fact: The plan includes securing federal databases, networks across all 50 states, and IT systems in over 3,000 counties, with a federal IT budget of about $74 billion
key_facts.excerpt: This massive effort includes securing federal databases, networks spanning all 50 states, and IT systems in over 3,000 counties. The federal government manages a massive IT budget of roughly $74 billion.

key_facts.fact: Days earlier, the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) signed agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI for voluntary pre-release model evaluations, joining existing Anthropic and OpenAI agreements
key_facts.excerpt: The Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) announced Tuesday that Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and Elon Musk's xAI have agreed to provide access to unreleased versions of their AI models for pre-deployment security and capability evaluations [...] Combined with existing—and recently renegotiated—agreements from Anthropic and OpenAI, every major U.S. frontier AI lab now participates in voluntary pre-release government evaluations.

key_facts.fact: CAISI has completed more than 40 model assessments to date, sometimes receiving versions of models with safety guardrails reduced to probe for national security risks
key_facts.excerpt: CAISI has completed more than 40 model assessments to date, including evaluations of unreleased state-of-the-art systems. Notably, developers sometimes hand over versions of their models with safety guardrails reduced specifically so the Center can probe for national security risks.
